title: Competitive Market Behavior of LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2609.02580v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as economic agents, yet there is little evidence whether LLM agents are suited for participating in market mechanisms designed for humans, and whether these mechanisms deliver desired outcomes when faced with LLM agents. We address this question by replicating seminal economic experiments, replacing human subjects with LLM agents. We place agents in a double auction environment, which is a widely-used market mechanism. We check whether such a market is able to deliver an efficient allocation of resources, thereby testing a novel dimension of alignment of LLM agents -- their compatibility with a fundamental market mechanism. We find that markets populated by LLM agents exhibit slower or no convergence towards market equilibrium, thus providing less efficient allocations than markets populated by humans. translated_title: 大语言模型的竞争性市场行为
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）正越来越多地被部署为经济主体（智能体），然而，关于LLM智能体是否适合参与为人类设计的市场机制，以及当面对LLM智能体时这些机制能否产生预期的结果，目前几乎没有相关证据。我们通过复制经典经济学实验来回答这一问题，用LLM智能体替代人类受试者。我们将智能体置于双向拍卖环境中，这是一种被广泛使用的市场机制。我们检验这样的市场能否实现资源的有效配置，从而测试了LLM智能体对齐的一个新维度——它们与基础市场机制的兼容性。我们发现，由LLM智能体组成的市场向市场均衡的收敛速度更慢，甚至无法收敛，因此其资源配置效率低于由人类组成的市场。随后，我们分析了智能体的个体交易决策，发现存在显著的异质性……
tldr: 该论文通过用LLM智能体替代人类复制经典的双向拍卖市场实验，首次发现由LLM组成的市场收敛到均衡的速度更慢甚至无法收敛，资源配置效率低于人类市场，并由此提出了LLM对齐的一个新维度——与基础市场机制的兼容性。
en_tdlr: By replicating classic double-auction market experiments with LLM agents replacing human subjects, this paper shows that LLM-populated markets exhibit slower or no convergence to equilibrium and yield less efficient allocations than human markets, introducing a novel alignment dimension: the compatibility of LLMs with fundamental market mechanisms.
